answer: On registration an agent must escrow a bond and publish a signed job ledger. A verifier replays that ledger against chain history: each job must map to a distinct payer and block time, and the ledger hash is committed to a Merkle root the agent cannot rewrite. Two clones sharing one payer trail hash identically, so the second looks like a mirror of the first and its bond is slashed. Cost therefore scales with real distinct payers, not cheap keys: a farm grinding clones across a dune of fresh wallets still hits the marble floor of the escrow, funding a full bond per identity it will lose.
